gloss: inari sushi; sushi rice in fried tofu pouches

definitions.gloss: inari sushi; sushi rice stuffed in sweetened fried tofu pouches
definitions.explanation: A type of sushi consisting of vinegared rice packed inside pouches of deep-fried tofu (abura-age) that have been simmered in a sweet soy sauce mixture. A popular, affordable everyday sushi often found at convenience stores and bento shops.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{弁当|べんとう}→お弁当：02864_obentou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{稲荷寿司|いなりずし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れた→入れる：01098_ireru⟧。
examples.english: I put inari sushi in the lunch box.

notes:
USAGE:
Named after the Shinto deity ⟦{稲荷|いなり}→稲荷：17450_inari⟧, whose fox messengers are said to be fond of fried tofu. Often shortened to おいなりさん in casual speech, with the honorific さん reflecting affection for the food. It is one of the most common types of sushi eaten at home and is a staple of bento culture.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- おいなりさん (casual/affectionate name for inari sushi)
- {稲荷寿司|いなりずし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧ (to make inari sushi)
- ⟦{油揚|あぶらあ}げ→油揚げ：07477_aburaage⟧ (fried tofu pouch — the main wrapping ingredient)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{手巻|てま}き{寿司|ずし}→手巻き寿司：15996_temakizushi⟧: hand-rolled sushi — another casual, home-style sushi
- ⟦{巻|ま}き{寿司|ずし}→巻き寿司：12410_makizushi⟧: rolled sushi — nori-wrapped cylindrical sushi
